messages:
Sanjay Rao: Microcanary popped 3 unexpected admin grants into payments-prod-admins during the weekly access-sweep. 2 grants look like console-driven, 1 via service account. Not sure if tied to the recent rollout. Can we triage and lock down?

Tara Lin: on it — grabbing audit logs and KMS grant history now. ETA ~15m. any suspected request IDs?

Sanjay Rao: no request IDs in the alert, just timestamp ranges and actor IDs (partial): svc-pay-ops, alice.g. Might be a manual emergency grant.

Kevin Park: I'll look at the approvals flow and check the admin-requests queue. If it was a manual console grant we should be able to see the IAM principal and the UI session id.

Tara Lin: pulled logs. snippets: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=AccessKeyId,AttributeValue=AKIA... --max-results 50``` and ```aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/kms/payments --start-time 1710000000000 --end-time 1710086400000``` — found a KMS:CreateGrant by arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/svc-pay-ops at 03:12 UTC.

Alex G: svc-pay-ops is a long-lived ops role but shouldn't be able to create admin grants against payments keyring. sounds like an RBAC drift. did we roll any role updates in the last 48h?

Maya (eng-security): I see a PR merged yesterday that adjusted Policies:PaymentsOps -> allowed kms:CreateGrant for cross-account rotation. Looks like scope was too broad. I'll link the PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/8321

Kevin Park: confirmed — PR 8321 added kms:CreateGrant with Resource: * by mistake. we should revoke the grant and issue a scoped follow-up. rollback plan: 1) revoke active grants from CreateGrant call (Tara) 2) patch policy to resource-specific ARNs (Maya) 3) rotate any keys where grants were used for new principals (Sanjay) 4) evidence capture and access-review note (Alex)

Oncall Bot: Incident INC-5812 created (severity: medium) — linked to thread 4812345678.

Tara Lin: revoked the 3 grants (aws kms retire-grant / aws kms revoke-grant) and exported the events to s3://redwood-sec/tmp/microcanary-4812345678.json. uploaded.

Maya (eng-security): patch submitted to fix the policy scope, tests added to prevent wildcard kms resources. PR 8330. requesting an expedited review.

Alex G: I'm starting a quick least-priv audit for payments-prod-admins group — will enumerate explicit grants and flag any non-owners. plan to have a CSV by EOD.

Sanjay Rao: good. capture requestor evidence & business justification for any persistent access. If none, schedule removal in next entitlement prune window. Also schedule a retro to tighten policy review for infra PRs touching KMS.

Tara Lin: saved log exports and KMS grant digests to the incident ticket. added actionable commands for SOC to replay if needed.

Kevin Park: I'll update the incident playbook with the rollback steps and add a quick smoke test for payments workload to ensure no regression after revocation.

Maya (eng-security): merging PR 8330 after security + infra thumbs. keeping canary on for 24h to watch for related regressions.

Alex G: CSV exported, 4 out-of-scope principals flagged (two service accounts, two human). opening access-review items and assigning owners.

Sanjay Rao: thanks team. closing fast but will keep audit evidence attached. follow-ups: add policy linter rule for kms resource wildcards, expand microcanary rules to include CreateGrant, and run cross-account grant inventory next week. :thumbsup:
